commands.review_summary:
Adds an 803-line draft RFC proposing a read-only `openclaw catalog` CLI/JSON inventory over command/tool surfaces, plugin descriptors, source-registry metadata, and prompt/audit/operator lenses.

Reproducibility: not applicable. this is a draft RFC feature/API proposal rather than a reported current-main bug. I verified current main lacks the `0016` catalog RFC and the PR adds only the design document.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] Manual review is needed because accepting a new core CLI/catalog and plugin metadata contract is a maintainer product/API decision, not a safe repair-lane task.

target.title: RFC 0016: CLI catalog view for command surfaces
target.body:
## What this RFC is proposing

This RFC proposes a read-only `openclaw catalog` view over OpenClaw's existing command/tool surfaces. The goal is one normalized inventory that can be viewed through scoped lenses: operator review, audit/compliance planning, generated docs, smoke-test planning, and a small prompt projection for bounded mechanical operations.

The catalog is metadata only. It is not a new dispatcher, policy engine, runtime hook, gateway plugin, or expression language. Existing commands, tools, plugins, and node surfaces continue to own validation, permissions, confirmation, execution, and results.

## Draft status and proof

This is still a draft RFC. It should not merge as accepted until maintainers choose the public CLI/API boundary and the RFC lifecycle is complete. The file is candidate `0016` to avoid the visible `0010` collision with other open RFC PRs.

Implementation evidence lives on the linked OpenClaw draft PR, not in this RFC repository: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100960. That branch has catalog unit coverage, generated fixture checks, generated docs checks, formatting checks, and branch-level review passes. If maintainers want a separate `maintainer-discussion` thread beyond this PR discussion, I can add that link before acceptance.

## What this adds to source registries

The source-registry addition is intentionally small and compliance-oriented: a command/tool can report its operational effect consistently wherever it appears.

```ts
type CommandEffectProfile = {
  effectMode: "read" | "mutating" | "mixed";
  confirmationRequired?: boolean;
  risk?: "low" | "medium" | "high";
  commandHints?: readonly string[];
};

type CatalogExposure = {
  tier?: "public" | "internal";
};
```

`CommandEffectProfile` answers whether a surface reads state, mutates state, or mixes both; whether callers should expect a confirmation boundary; what risk level audit/operator views should assume; and what concise command hints help humans or prompt projections choose the right existing command.

`CatalogExposure` answers only whether the entry is suitable for public catalog/docs output or should stay internal by default. It is not a per-consumer allowlist. Choices like docs vs prompt vs audit vs operator belong in catalog lenses. Plugin descriptors may also carry `hidden` for private/local placeholders that generated views should omit unless explicitly requested.

That gives compliance and operators a consistent answer across CLI routes, plugin commands, runtime commands, and node/operator commands without moving enforcement into the catalog. CLI descriptors still own command shape, route entries still own routing/policy shape, plugin descriptors still own plugin command shape, and node/operator commands come from node pairing/runtime declarations. The catalog builder normalizes those N sources into one view.

## Why this is useful

OpenClaw already has several bounded operational surfaces: CLI descriptors, command routes, routed operations, runtime Commander commands, plugin descriptors, tool-backed surfaces, and node/operator commands. Today those surfaces are partly discoverable through help text, registries, docs, prompt prose, and implementation details, but there is no single joined read-only inventory that answers:

- what command/tool surfaces exist
- where each entry came from
- whether it mutates state or needs confirmation
- whether it is public catalog material or internal-only by default
- which entries should appear in audit, docs, prompt, or operator lenses

The catalog keeps existing registries as the source of truth and adds the missing joined view over them.

## Complexity this makes inspectable

The implementation review branch already inventories 61 CLI descriptors, 97 command routes, 14 routed operations, 5 explicit agent/tool surfaces, and node/operator command metadata. The audit/report layer groups that same inventory by state-changing vs read-only/mixed effects, confirmation-required surfaces, route policy keys, routes missing policy keys, routed-operation smoke-test coverage gaps, node/operator commands, and approval-required node commands.

This is not just a static help dump. `openclaw catalog list` collects the live Commander tree for the current invocation, and `openclaw catalog list --plugin-descriptors` also includes plugin-provided CLI descriptor metadata when that metadata is explicitly requested. That distinction matters because plugin and Scout deployments are not fixed static lists. In the Scout container proof, the same inventory idea already sees 13 plugins, 11 enabled plugins, 2 plugin CLI commands, 8 plugin tools, and 23 allowed command/tool names from the loaded config.

## Output field budget

The current implementation explores several output entry kinds with rough field counts: descriptors about 9 fields, command routes about 8, routed operations about 5, runtime commands about 13, plugin commands about 17, node/operator commands about 20, and prompt projection entries about 9.

That does not all need to become the minimum stable output contract. The first stable `catalog list --json` contract can be much smaller: identity, provenance, exposure tier, and safety summary. Fields like examples, aliases, command hints, effects, owner, status, confidence, policy keys, approval kind, trust boundary, and node-specific availability should stay advisory or lens-specific until a concrete consumer proves they are worth carrying.

## Minimum useful slice

If the full lens stack feels too large for a first pass, the minimum useful outcome is the core catalog integration plus the `openclaw catalog` command/JSON contract. That alone gives Scout a stable inventory surface it can consume right away for compliance, auditability, plugin review, and operator diagnostics. OpenClaw can then adopt the richer prompt, docs, audit, coverage, and node/operator lenses over time, as shown in the draft implementation stack, without requiring all of those consumers to land up front.

## Scope boundaries

This should stay additive and low-risk:

- no new execution path
- no policy enforcement in the catalog itself
- no dumping the full inventory into prompts
- no force-loading arbitrary plugin runtime code for discovery
- no public plugin SDK commitment in the first pass

The first implementation should expose a CLI/JSON contract such as `openclaw catalog list --json`, then let docs, prompt projection, audit, coverage, and operator summaries consume that same metadata.

## Implementation review links

RFC file: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/rfcs/blob/codex/cli-catalog-overlay-rfc/rfcs/0016-cli-catalog-overlay.md

There is one upstream draft PR with the full end-state branch:

- Rollup implementation PR: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100960

For easier review, the same work is also split into fork-local draft PRs. These are review aids, not a request to merge from the fork. I am happy to open the same stack directly against `openclaw/openclaw` if maintainers want to review/merge it that way.

- PR1 foundation: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/11
- PR2 dynamic/operator lenses: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/12
- PR3 prompt projection: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/13
- PR4 schema fixtures: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/14
- PR5 generated docs: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/15
- PR6 hardening/consumer contract: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/16

## Feedback requested

The most useful feedback is on the shape and boundary:

- should this be a core `openclaw catalog` command, a plugin-provided surface, or a hybrid where plugins contribute metadata to a core read-only view?
- are `CommandEffectProfile` and `CatalogExposure` the right minimal source-registry structs?
- is `CatalogExposure.tier = public | internal` the right terminology, with `hidden` as a separate omit marker?
- should catalog avoid source-registry additions entirely at first and rely only on derived/overlay data?
- what minimum dynamic/plugin/node data should the first command include?
- are the proposed lenses useful: prompt, audit, test matrix, generated docs, operator summary?

If the direction is too broad, I can narrow the first PR to the smallest useful read-only inventory and leave prompt/audit/docs lenses as later PRs.
